title: McsB Regulates CtsR Thermosensing Through Peripheral Arginine Phosphorylation.
authors: Cai, Huahuan; Hua, Boyang; Hu, Jie; Fu, Yiben; Liu, Shuting; Ding, Xinlei; Duan, Gege; Guo, Yeting; Xia, Xing-Hua; Zhao, Yufen
one_liner_zh: 该文通过单分子荧光和结构模拟研究细菌转录抑制因子CtsR与DNA的动态互作及McsB磷酸化调控机制，虽聚焦TF-DNA体系且含结构模拟，但方法以实验为主、AI/物理模拟深度有限，故为中档匹配。
abstract: When cells sense an elevated temperature in the environment, the bacterial master transcription repressor CtsR becomes phosphorylated and inactivated by the arginine kinase McsB to initiate the expression of heat-shock genes. Here, we utilize a fluorescence intensity shift assay (FISA) based on the photoisomerisation-related fluorescence enhancement (or previously protein-induced fluorescence enhancement, PIFE) effect to monitor the DNA-CtsR-McsB interactions in real time. Our single-molecule analysis reveals that CtsR binds rapidly and stably to the cognate DNA, and that McsB is able to transiently interact with CtsR in situ of the target DNA. We determine the binding kinetics between McsB and the DNA-bound CtsR by single-molecule real-time binding assays, with k(on) and k(off) of 0.75 muM(-1) s(-1) and 0.34 s(-1), respectively. This interaction with McsB does not remove CtsR from the DNA, but lowers the temperature threshold for CtsR dissociation and alters its thermosensing behavior. Mass spectrometry, mutational analysis and structural simulation results together suggest that the phosphorylation of several peripheral arginine residues on CtsR, which reduces the binding energy of the CtsR-DNA complex, underlies a plausible molecular mechanism for this effect. Taken together, these results provide insights into how McsB regulates the CtsR-DNA interaction and highlight the functional importance of CtsR peripheral arginine residues in the bacterial heat-shock response.
abstract_zh: 当细胞感知到环境温度升高时，细菌主转录抑制因子CtsR被精氨酸激酶McsB磷酸化并失活，从而启动热休克基因的表达。在此，我们利用基于光异构化相关荧光增强（或先前称为蛋白质诱导荧光增强，PIFE）效应的荧光强度位移测定法（FISA），实时监测DNA-CtsR-McsB相互作用。我们的单分子分析揭示，CtsR快速且稳定地结合至同源DNA，且McsB能够在靶DNA原位与CtsR发生瞬时相互作用。我们通过单分子实时结合测定确定了McsB与DNA结合态CtsR之间的结合动力学，其k(on)和k(off)分别为0.75 μM⁻¹ s⁻¹和0.34 s⁻¹。与McsB的这种相互作用并未将CtsR从DNA上移除，而是降低了CtsR解离的温度阈值，并改变了其热感应行为。质谱分析、突变分析和结构模拟结果共同表明，CtsR上多个外围精氨酸残基的磷酸化降低了CtsR-DNA复合物的结合能，这可能是该效应的分子机制基础。综合来看，这些结果揭示了McsB如何调控CtsR-DNA相互作用，并强调了CtsR外围精氨酸残基在细菌热休克反应中的功能重要性。
